hints.title: State Representation by Difference
hints.text: An arithmetic subsequence is uniquely parameterized by its common difference d. Define the state as the maximum length ending at index i with step difference d.

hints.title: Transition Across Prior Elements
hints.text: For each pair of indices j < i, the difference is d = nums[i] - nums[j]. Transition by extending the chain ending at j: dp[i][d] = dp[j][d] + 1, defaulting to 1 + 1.

hints.title: Iterative DP Filling
hints.text: Populate states for each i from left to right. Maintain an array of dictionaries or an offset array. Track the global maximum length across all transitions and return it.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all subsequences is exponential O(2^N), which times out for N = 1000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tabulating lengths indexed by (index, difference) runs in quadratic time and quadratic space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should model the state as DP[index][diff] and optimize lookups with hash tables or flat arrays.
complexity.notes: Differences can be negative, spanning from -500 to 500 given element range [0, 500].
